claims: Each leg has distance d, so its time is d/u or d/v. Dividing total distance by total time gives 2/(1/u+1/v). With d=3 km and speeds 3 and 6 km/h, the average is 4 km/h. Equal-time travel instead gives the arithmetic mean.
Opening and worked traversals use a two-to-one duration ratio. Later bars represent time, not distance. This is a kinematic example, not advice to rush.
limitations: Numerical checks complement the stated derivation; idealizations are explicit.
